## The Power of "Global" Models

### The Challenge
The **M5 Competition** (2020) was the "Olympics of Forecasting," hosted by Walmart.
*   **Task:** Forecast daily sales for **30,490** items across 10 stores (300,000+ time series) for 28 days.
*   **Difficulty:** Many items are "intermittent" (sell 0 on most days, then 1 or 2).

### The Win: LightGBM & Cross-Learning
The classic approach would be to build 30,000 separate ARIMA models (one for each product). **No top competitor did this.**
The winner (a student) used **LightGBM** (Gradient Boosted Trees) to build a **Global Model**.
*   **Method:** He fed ALL 30,000 products into a *single* massive model.
*   **Why it worked:** **Cross-Learning.** A bag of chips in Store A behaves similarly to a bag of pretzels in Store B. The model learned "weekend spikes" and "price drop effects" from high-volume items and applied those lessons to low-volume items that didn't have enough history to learn on their own.

### The Lesson
**Don't isolate your data.**
In modern forecasting (Retail, SaaS, Web Traffic), **Global Models** (training on many series at once) almost always beat Local Models (one series at a time). They "borrow strength" from the whole dataset.
